pairs.subject: embedded-db
pairs.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:9 The only store-writing script in this context tells you to raw-copy a single-writer PGlite directory while the dev server holds it, which yields a torn copy that still carries the holder's postmaster.pid. That bypasses the repo's own storeCopy.ts rules, and it routes the materialized vote_tag writes into a throwaway copy instead of the canonical store.

techniques.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:8 Exactly the failure the technique names: copying a held store instead of holding the connection, checkpointing and stripping the lock marker. lib/db/pglite/storeCopy.ts calls such a copy 'torn by construction'. Explicit close (line 134) and explicit process.exit (line 146) are conformant, but they do not cure the copy instruction.

scripts/hybrid-bench/run.ts:28 The benchmark arms (run/agg/derived/join) read flat JSON exports, not the serving store, and they are small LLM-operator benches, not user-perceptible aggregates. The README plans to move the 406k-ballot reads to PGlite via the Store 'when this graduates', and that move would trigger this technique.
scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:90 A one-shot script that takes the single PGlite handle once. There is no pool in this context, and pool sizing lives in lib/db.

scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:119 vote_tag rows are upserted by a per-vote id, so the table is bounded by the vote count and does not accumulate. Store-wide accounting lives in lib/db/pglite/accounting.ts, outside this context. The .pglite-mat copy directory the comment creates has no named reaper either.

pairs.registryProposal: The analytical-reads technique uses 'an analysis script carrying an instruction to run against a copy' as its signature, but here the script carrying that instruction is a WRITER that materializes product data. For a writer the copy workaround is worse than contention: the writes land in a throwaway copy and silently never reach the canonical store. single-writer-holder-discipline could name 'writes routed to a copy' as a distinct failure from 'a torn backup'.
